in_greek.name: Βεβις
in_greek.long_meaning: The name Bevis in Greek is derived from the Greek word 'bios' meaning 'man' and the suffix '-is' meaning 'of'. Thus, Bevis in Greek can be translated to 'man of God'.

in_latin.name: Bevisius
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Bevisius in Latin is derived from Bevis and the suffix '-ius' meaning 'living or belonging to'. Thus, Bevisius in Latin can be translated to 'living or belonging to Bevis'.

in_english.name: Bevis
in_english.long_meaning: The name Bevis in English is derived from Old English 'beof' or 'beofa' which means beo, god, and 'wis' or 'friend' meaning wise or friend. Thus, Bevis in English can be translated to 'beo-wise' or 'god-wise' or 'friend of God'.

data.cultural_impact: Bevis is a rare name in modern English speaking cultures, but it was popular during the Middle Ages. It is said that St. Bevis was a British saint who lived during the 7th century. The name has been associated with nobility and bravery in medieval literature, particularly in the chivalric epic "Bevis of Hampton." This tale follows a young man named Bevis who goes on a series of adventures and ultimately becomes a knight. The name Bevis carries a sense of courage and prestige, linked to the romanticized ideals of the Middle Ages and the chivalric code of honor.
